gap: No result ChatGPT got states that xTool's own M2 FAQ says 'xTool M2 is not compatible with LightBurn or XCS': the top pick runs only on xTool Studio. It also does not state that LightBurn's developer said on 2026-09-30 that its driver doesn't fully support the budget Falcon A1C yet.
standout_why: I compared against maker-wise.com (cited). Its M2 entry says nothing about software. It only says in general that 'xTool and Glowforge work best in their own apps' and that 'LightBurn Core costs $99 and is worth it once you run more than one machine', so it covers part of this and never says the M2 is locked out. ChatGPT's own answer gives 'LightBurn compatibility' as a Falcon A1 plus but says nothing about the M2 or A1C. I could not read Tom's Hardware (cited) or the xTool beginner guide (cited): WebFetch returned only their titles, so I couldn't check them for this point.
decides: This confirms the M2 as the easiest first machine for someone who stays in the maker's app. It does not remove the M2 as a pick. It does decide the pick for a beginner who wants to move up to LightBurn later or run a second machine in one program: xTool says the M2 is locked to xTool Studio, so the Falcon A1 10W fits that plan. Don't push the A1C as the LightBurn-ready budget option, because LightBurn's own developer says A1C support is incomplete and framing over Wi-Fi failed in a user's test.

findings.label: Software compatibility
findings.value: "xTool M2 is not compatible with LightBurn or XCS." Compatible software: xTool Studio (Windows/macOS)
findings.note: Maker's support FAQ, which shows an update date of Nov 5, 2026. A third-party manual site (notice-facile.com) lists LightBurn as compatible. The maker's own statement takes precedence.

findings.label: Offline operation limit
findings.value: Can run without the software connected, but offline it "can only process the task last executed on the device"
findings.note: Connects over USB or Wi-Fi, per the same FAQ.

findings.label: Laser class and blue-module wavelength
findings.value: Class 1; 445 nm ±15 nm (10/20/40 W blue modules); optional 3 W 1,064 nm IR module
findings.note: The FAQ says the blue module 'is not suitable for processing highly reflective materials, such as mirror-finished metals, unoxidized aluminum, copper, and mirror-finished stainless steel.'

findings.label: LightBurn driver status
findings.value: LightBurn developer Jeremy Lee, 2026-09-30: "we haven't updated the driver to support the A1C fully yet"; "Console GCode and User Macros will NOT work on any of the Falcons over HTTP"
findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1C support - LightBurn Software Forum
findings.note: The user (zyberbob, 2026-09-29) connected an A1C 10W over Wi-Fi with the 'Creality Falcon' HTTP device type. Home and jog worked; Frame did not. LightBurn forum staff member Aaron.F (2026-10-09) suggested the GRBL device type as the workaround 'until we get Creality's feedback about the API differences for the A1C.'
